discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 111728
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
1228 PM EST Wed Nov 11 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Rain showers develop and spread across the area this afternoon
  and early evening. An isolated thunderstorm is possible across
  portions of northwest Indiana this afternoon and early evening
  with isolated wind gusts of over 40 mph possible with any 
  showers or isolated storms.

- Lake effect showers impact areas mainly west of US-31 in
  northwest Indiana and far southwest Lower Michigan Thursday
  through Friday night. Snow is expected to mix in by late 
  Thursday night into Friday morning. Additional lake effect 
  snow showers are possible early Saturday. Some slushy snow 
  accumulations are possible with the lake effect, mainly early 
  Friday morning across northwest Indiana. 

- Below normal temperatures Thursday through this weekend before
  moderating midweek next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1200 PM EST Wed Nov 11 2026

A vigorous shortwave continues moving southeast from IA this morning 
through Central IL today, reaching central IN this afternoon. The 
eventual placement of the warm front will be key in understanding 
severity, but there appears to be some southward trend in that 
placement in models between yesterday and today. Key to thunderstorm 
development appears to be the mid level lapse rates. Hail was 
forming across eastern IA this morning right on the northern 
gradient from high to low within an elevated area of instability. 
This would be the cause of hail should it form across the area 
today. Such an area of mid level lapse rates moves into areas south 
of US-30 midday into the afternoon before vacating by 20z. This area 
is well out in front of the forcing and would likely not be where 
storms form. The other area into our southwest 1 to 2 tiers of 
counties has mid level lapse rates from 6.5 to 7C. This overlaps 
with an area of very weak MUCAPE right around 100 to 250 J/kg in the 
20 to 00z window. There is some low level turning to work with 
within the lowest 1 to 2km of the atmosphere, but given the weak 
instability and what appears to be an elevated instability nature to 
the atmospheric column, the tornado threat appears to be low unless 
we can realize a taller surface instability column. Soundings appear 
to show a sort of an onion-shaped or shallow inverted-V profile that 
may be conducive to bringing winds down to the surface alluding to 
the gusty to damaging wind possibility. 

Hot on the heels of this wave is an area of vorticity traveling 
southward from Canada. As this area travels southward, it
deepens and interacts with the departing low pressure area. 
What's interesting is the deeper cold is delayed and farther 
west of Lk MI on Thursday. The ECMWF almost has a drainage 
signal where the eastern Lk MI area is cold, but over the lake 
is warmer, even at 850 mb. So, while the QPF signal appears lake
effect/lake enhanced, we haven't gotten the cold air enough to 
change it over to snow yet. A couple of compact waves traverse 
southward nearby Lk MI and the RRFS seems to show a trough 
kicking off a more sustained band Thursday evening. By the time 
we get to early Fri AM, enough cold air has wrapped in that 
soundings are beginning to get snow mixed in or changed over. -5
to -6C at 850 mb is right over the southern tear drop of Lk MI 
on the ECMWF so that makes sense. As various waves/instability 
troughs traverse southward, finding the exact trajectory will be
difficult because there will be some east-west wavering. A 
slight eastward change can mean the relatively vigorous lift 
going on from the relatively warm lake and cold airmass 
interaction can mean quick snow rates getting into LaPorte and 
maybe Starke counties. These could be rates that overcome the 
warm ground from how anomalously warm we've been this late fall.
As such, will continue the mention of the 1 to 2 inches of snow
through Friday that could result in LaPorte county especially 
with that wavering. Model guidance with variable snow ratios 
continues to back this up. It'll be interesting to see what 
happens with snow and if it'll stay mainly on grassy surfaces or
if it'll have enough oomph to accumulate on roads. Some 
guidance say it'll struggle to accumulate on roads Friday 
morning. The snow band may push eastward Saturday morning toward
US-30, but it would appear to be more diffuse at that point and
in its dying trend. It'll also trend back to rain or drizzle as
the column warms. Lake clouds could continue through Sunday 
with the northwest trajectories continuing. It is interesting to
see the highs are still forecast to warm into the 40s on Friday
and Saturday. That would cut into the accumulation ceilings and
I'm curious if we'd have refreezing overnight with sub-freezing
lows. This would depend on having standing water left on roads 
that, with light to calm wind, would indicate it's possible. 

Finally, by the time we get to Monday, trajectories change even as 
the last vigorous wave traverses the lake Saturday. Surface high 
pressure is already working to dry low level moisture out this 
weekend. Highs trend warmer through the 40s to reach the 50s by the 
middle of next week as the surface high slowly translates eastward. 
There is a vigorous wave south of the high that moves into the Gulf 
States, but it's far enough south to avoid our area. The warm 
advection pattern returns midweek next week as a wave shifts 
northeastward from the Central Plains into south-central Canada. As 
a result, the work week looks dry Monday through at least Thursday. 
However, lows won't rise above freezing until Thursday morning.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z THURSDAY/...
Issued at 1222 PM EST Wed Nov 11 2026

A complex of scattered showers and storms north of a frontal 
boundary in northern IA and IL is moving west towards northwest
Indiana this afternoon. Winds will shift from the southeast to
northeast later this afternoon as showers arrive. Scattered
light to moderate rain showers will move through late this 
afternoon and evening, with MVFR ceilings and visibilities 
expected at both KSBN and KFWA. Peak chances for showers will 
occur from 22-00Z tonight at KSBN and from 00-02Z tonight at 
KFWA. With cyclonic, northwest flow developing tonight and 
overnight, ceilings will be prevailing MVFR at least through 
Thursday morning as additional clouds advect in off of Lake 
Michigan. Lake effect showers quickly develop in response 
following the frontal passage. There may be a brief lull in 
showers at KSBN between 02-06Z for a few hours before starting 
up again after 06Z Thursday morning.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory from 7 PM this evening to 7 AM EST 
     Saturday for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Roller
AVIATION...Johnson

Isolated severe thunderstorms are also possible across the east-central Florida Peninsula.
spc.text:
SPC AC 111630

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1030 AM CST Wed Nov 11 2026

   Valid 111630Z - 121200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   THE LOWER OHIO AND WESTERN TENNESSEE VALLEYS...AS WELL AS ACROSS THE
   EAST-CENTRAL FLORIDA PENINSULA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms capable of producing isolated hail, damaging winds,
   and perhaps a tornado may occur this afternoon and evening across
   parts of eastern Illinois into Indiana, western/central Kentucky,
   and middle Tennessee. Isolated severe thunderstorms are also
   possible across the east-central Florida Peninsula.

   ...Midwest/Lower Ohio Valley into Middle Tennessee...
   Recent satellite imagery shows a lead shortwave trough moving into
   northern IL, with another shortwave trough farther back northwest
   moving into the Mid MO Valley. Showers and thunderstorms are ongoing
   near the lead shortwave. Thunderstorm intensity has decreased over
   the last half hour or so as these storms move into an environment
   with less elevated buoyancy (as observed by the 12Z ILX sounding).
   The lead shortwave is forecast to continue eastward into the OH
   Valley while the second shortwave continues more southeastward into
   the Lower OH Valley vicinity. The surface low currently over the
   IA/IL border vicinity is forecast to progress eastward with the lead
   wave while an attendant cold front sweeps southeastward through the
   mid MS Valley/Mid-South, and lower OH Valley this afternoon and
   evening.

   Increasing low-level moisture is anticipated ahead of this front,
   advecting northeastward into the region from the Ozarks/Mid-South
   region. Recent surface analysis shows the mid 50s dewpoints are
   still in northern AR, so there is some question as to how far
   northeastward the greater low-level moisture will reach before
   frontal passage. Current expectation is for the best overlap between
   low-level moisture (and associated buoyancy) with the stronger
   large-scale ascent will occur across southern IN and adjacent
   western KY. Here, the combination of weak buoyancy (i.e. MLCAPE
   around 500-800 J/kg) and 30-40 kt of deep-layer shear
   oriented largely orthogonal to the surface cold front should support
   a mix of bowing clusters and supercells. Isolated hail and damaging
   gusts will be the primary risks. Hail is more likely with any more
   cellular activity and damaging gusts more likely with any
   fast-moving bowing segments. Modestly enhanced low-level
   shear may also support a low-probability tornado risk, but a
   tendency for low-level flow to veer to westerly should reduce
   effective SRH with time through the late afternoon/evening. The
   isolated severe risk should diminish with eastward extent this
   evening across the lower OH Valley as front outruns the low-level
   moisture and daytime heating wanes.

   ...Central/Southern Florida Peninsula...
   Isolated to scattered thunderstorms are expected across the 
   central/southern FL Peninsula this afternoon. Glancing large-scale
   ascent associated with a weak mid-level perturbation over the
   Southeast should aid this convective development. A warm layer
   around 700 mb could limit overall buoyancy, but 500 mb temperatures
   will be around -9 to -11 deg C and most forecast sounding still show
   1500+ J/kg of uninhibited MLCAPE this afternoon. Moderate deep-layer
   shear will exists across the region as well. These conditions appear
   supportive of marginally severe hail and gusty winds within the
   stronger cores, which appear most probable along the east-central FL
   Coast.

   ..Mosier/Halbert-K.. 11/11/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 111730

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1130 AM CST Wed Nov 11 2026

   Valid 121200Z - 131200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FOR PORTIONS OF
   THE MID ATLANTIC...

   ...SUMMARY...
   A couple of damaging gusts or marginally severe hail may accompany
   one of the stronger storms across the Mid-Atlantic tomorrow
   (Thursday) afternoon.

   ...Synopsis...
   A broad upper trough will overspread the eastern U.S. while an upper
   ridge builds over the Rockies and pronounced mid-level impulse
   impinges on the CA coastline tomorrow (Thursday). A surface low will
   accompany the East Coast upper trough and traverse the Mid-Atlantic
   during the day. A surface cold front will sweep across the
   Mid-Atlantic, resulting in enough deep-layer ascent amid a
   marginally buoyant airmass to support scattered thunderstorm
   development, one or two of which may be severe. Surface high
   pressure and a stable low-level airmass will usher in behind the
   cold front over the most of the CONUS, limiting thunderstorm
   development.

   ...Portions of the Mid-Atlantic...
   A relatively cool low-level airmass (e.g. near 60 F surface
   temperatures) is expected across the Mid-Atlantic given scattered to
   widespread cloud cover and precipitation across the warm sector
   preceding the low. Nonetheless, 7+ C/km mid-level lapse rates will
   overspread mid 50s F surface dewpoints, amid minimal MLCINH,
   yielding up to 500 J/kg MLCAPE. Though stronger 500 mb flow will
   overspread VA into the Carolinas, strong enough southwesterly
   mid-level wind fields will yield 40+ kts of effective bulk shear.
   This low CAPE/moderate shear profile may support sustained
   multicells and transient supercells capable of producing strong to
   potentially damaging wind gusts and perhaps an instance of
   marginally severe hail tomorrow afternoon.

   ..Squitieri.. 11/11/2026

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0700Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 110827

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0227 AM CST Wed Nov 11 2026

   Valid 131200Z - 141200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe thunderstorms are forecast across the U.S. Friday and
   Friday night.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   An upper-level trough will move eastward across the Atlantic Coastal
   states Friday into Friday night, as a shortwave mid-level ridge
   moves into the High Plains. Further west, an upper-level trough will
   move onshore into the western U.S. on Friday. Thunderstorms will be
   possible ahead of this feature in parts of the Desert Southwest and
   near the trough along the coasts of northern California and
   southwest Oregon. No severe threat is forecast across the
   continental U.S. Friday and Friday night.

   ..Broyles.. 11/11/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
